summary:
Independent check of lane data-02 (D-DATA-02, format of the run inventory). Skills loaded: `ariakit-general-workflow`, `ariakit-general-code-style` (remote: `github.com/ariakit/visonaut`). The repository is unchanged; all checker files are in `/Users/diegohaz/.claude/jobs/f65a6229/tmp/round2/data-02/check/`.

**Confirmed.** I ran every probe of the first agent again. Each byte count and each memory number is identical (`rows-3832.json` is the same file). Times are within noise (complete real read 369 to 410 ms; rows 69 to 83 ms). The code facts (limit constant and throw, 1 writer and 6 readers, CLI 8 MiB, service 16 MiB and 40,000, 10,000 profiles), the D1 numbers (66 / 90 / 1,866), the contract lines, D54, pull requests #247 and #249, the Cloudflare limits, and the Ariakit pins are correct.

**Refuted or corrected (6).** The largest one: the fixture has only 4 changed captures of 3,832, and the claim "16 MiB hold 40,000 captures" depends on that. I made every capture a changed capture and the real writer accepted it:

```text
3,832 captures, all changed     today      rows (first prototype)   rows (nested difference)
inventory bytes                 13,540,316 8,260,887                3,461,390
bytes for each capture          3,533      2,156                    903
captures that 16 MiB hold       ~4,750     ~7,780                   ~18,800
```

The first prototype stored the complete metadata again for one new key (`maskImageId`). I measured a repaired copy (`check/pack-deep.ts`). Also: the prototype is not lossless for a baseline with no manifest (it returns an empty profile list; rows 1,763 bytes for each capture).

**Recommendation.** `capture-rows-from-cli` survives, with weaker numbers: it holds the 10,580 captures of the contract also when every capture changed (inventory 9.46 MB, request 7.14 MB), but not 20,000 such captures (17.85 MB, 106%). I added the option `capture-rows-cli-limits` (rows in the service and 2 CLI constants), which is the minimal way past 5,700 and stops at about 8,000 to 9,150. The decision now has 5 options and stays open.

**Files changed:** `content/sections/40-data-storage.html` (lane part only; head and tail are byte-identical to the original), `decisions.patch.json` and `content/decisions.json`, `notes.md` (new section "Independent check"). `terms.patch.json` is unchanged. Build `--strict` and `check.mjs` pass.

corrections.claim: With rows, the 16 MiB limit holds 40,000 captures, and the largest run of the recommended option is 40,000.
corrections.problem: True only for a run with few changes (the fixture has 4 changed captures of 3,832). I made every capture a changed capture (check/changed.probe.ts, validated by the real writeCaptureInventory). First prototype: 2,156 bytes for each changed capture, 8,260,887 bytes at 3,832 captures, so 16 MiB hold about 7,780. Reason: difference() in probe/pack.ts compares top keys only, so the new key metadata.localResult.maskImageId stores the complete metadata again. With a nested difference (check/pack-deep.ts, round trip equal up to 10,580): 903 bytes for each, 9,464,461 at 10,580, 17,850,967 at 20,000 (106.4%), about 18,800 captures in 16 MiB.
corrections.fix: Lead, option table, decision text, alert sentence now say: 40,000 when few captures changed, about 18,800 when every capture changed. New size table 'when every capture changed'. New third panel in the compare demo with a real changed row (862 bytes; 2,166 in the first prototype). Calculator has a new input 'Captures that changed' (0 to 100%) and all formulas use it.

corrections.claim: The inventory of today stops at about 5,260 captures and the manifest request at about 9,150.
corrections.problem: Both are for a run with few changes. Measured with the real writer: 13,540,316 bytes for 3,832 changed captures (80.7% of 16 MiB), so the inventory of today stops at about 4,750 captures that all changed. The manifest request of today is 7,998,732 bytes in that case, so its stop is about 8,000.
corrections.fix: The stops table has a new column 'Stops at about, every capture changed' (4,750 / 5,700 / 8,000 / 10,600 / 40,000). The option keep-format-refuse-early names 4,750. Added the estimate: at 19 captures each day, a run has 5,260 captures in about 74 days.

corrections.claim: The imported baseline has no manifest: the prototype keeps its facts, but its rows are not short.
corrections.problem: Measured (check/imported.probe.ts): the round trip fails on the field profiles. unpackInventory collects profiles only when a manifest header exists (probe/pack.ts:498), so the list comes back empty. The rows have 6,754,138 bytes at 3,832 captures (1,763 for each).
corrections.fix: The text after the example and the item 'Not built and not measured' state the failure and the bytes, and that the product code must build the rows from the capture facts. The option capture-rows says that the prototype does not handle a baseline with no manifest. Also added the 10,000 capture limit of the import tool (apps/web/tooling/baseline-reset/reset.ts:32).

corrections.claim: The four options are the complete set; a CLI release that only raises constants is a rejected direction.
corrections.problem: It is the minimal way past 5,700 captures and materially different (2 constants, no new request format), but the section did not show it at all. The maintainer could not compare the recommended L option with the cheap one.
corrections.fix: New option capture-rows-cli-limits ('Rows in the service, and higher limits in the CLI') in decisions.patch.json, the section list, both tables, and the calculator. Measured bounds: about 9,150 captures, about 8,000 when every capture changed (request limit 16 MiB). It is not recommended, because it does not hold 10,580 and a higher request limit meets the isolate memory (79 MB at 10,580 in Node).

corrections.claim: Stored inventories need one conversion: one R2 write and one pointer update for each. No option adds a D1 write.
corrections.problem: The pointer update is a D1 write (run row and snapshot row). It is one time and not for each run, so standing rule 1 holds, but the text hid it. The draft also planned a migration of older runs, which the task excluded.
corrections.fix: The item 'Stored inventories' now says: no old run is converted; only the baseline needs the new form; way A keeps the reader of today for the baseline until the next main run replaces it (0 D1 writes); way B converts the baseline one time (1 R2 write, pointer update of 2 rows). It names what is lost (capture list of older runs, a run in review needs a new Submit) and that the recovery check needs a rule for old files.

corrections.claim: The image digest is in the file 6 times, and the profile digest 5 times.
corrections.problem: The profile digest of that capture is 9 times in the file, because a second capture has the same profile. It is 5 times in the four records of the capture.
corrections.fix: Text changed to 'The four records hold the image digest 6 times and the profile digest 5 times.'

corrections.claim: Limits that stay with capture-rows-from-cli: the 40,000 captures and the memory of the isolate.
corrections.problem: Three limits were not named. (1) The 16 MiB constant stays and the write above it still throws with the same bad failure. (2) apps/web/src/capture-inventory.ts:186 and :368 check 10,000 profiles on the inventory too. (3) The manifest file of each capture job has an indent of 2 and the same 8 MiB limit: the Linux job (2,632 captures) is at about 66.6% and passes 10,000 profiles at about 15,400 captures in the run (estimate). Also: a review read of two inventories as rows is 97 MB at 40,000 captures in Node.
corrections.fix: New cost item 'The limit stays a constant' (alert and early refusal stay necessary). The stops table names capture-inventory.ts:186 and the capture job file. The option table and the memory paragraph name the 15,400 estimate and the 97 MB.

corrections.claim: A complete read with all checks is 73 ms with rows in place of 385 ms.
corrections.problem: Three runs gave 69 to 83 ms for the rows (profile digests 57, 67, 71 ms) and 369 to 410 ms for today. One number hid the spread, and the 27-read estimate did not say Node.
corrections.fix: Text and decision say 'about 75 ms in place of about 385 ms', with the ranges, and 'in Node' on the CPU estimate.

corrections.claim: Sizes table of the options, and wording of the part.
corrections.problem: The size table was wider than its box at 1440 px (cells cut off). The words 'the lane' and 'A Worker has no line reader for JSON' were unclear for the maintainer. The lead said 'two parts' for three items.
corrections.fix: Both size tables now have the same shape (file, options by number, three counts) and fit. 'the lane' became 'this round'; the stream claim became 'no built-in reader for lines of JSON'; the lead says three parts and names the independent check.

recommendations.reason: It is the only option that holds the 10,580 captures of the contract in each measured case. Measured at 10,580 captures: inventory 4.28 MB (few changes) and 9.46 MB (every capture changed, 56.4% of 16 MiB); manifest request 2.80 MB and 7.14 MB. The other options stop at about 4,750 to 5,260 (keep), 5,700 (rows in the service, pages), and 8,000 to 9,150 (rows and higher CLI limits). No option adds a D1 write for a run: the recorded probe has 66 rows written and no statement holds a format fact. Each way past 5,700 needs the same CLI release and the same pull request in Ariakit (app.yml:11, :252, ci.yml:70). Its service part is the option capture-rows, which is measured and can ship first. This is a recommendation, not a decision: the decision stays open.
recommendations.wrongIf: About 8,000 captures are enough for the next year: then capture-rows-cli-limits is the simpler option (2 CLI constants). Or the count stays below about 5,000: then capture-rows alone is enough. Or a measurement in a Worker shows much more memory than Node for a read of rows at 10,580 or 20,000 captures (Node: 12.8 MB and 24.2 MB for one capture list). Or a build of the CLI part shows that the manifest digest and the signed evidence cannot use the rows without the long form in the Worker (73.7 MB of text at 40,000 captures). Or real changed captures need much more than about 890 bytes for each row.

remainingDoubts: Nothing ran in workerd. All times and memory numbers are from Node v24.18.0 on one laptop. The memory of a run in which every capture changed was not measured in any runtime.

The CLI part of the recommended option is not built. The way to calculate the manifest digest with no long form in the Worker is not designed (digest of the rows, or the digest of today calculated piece by piece). This is the largest doubt of the recommendation.

The changed captures of my measurement are synthetic, in the form of the 4 changed captures of the fixture. Real changed captures can have other result fields. The 890 bytes come from my repaired copy of the prototype, which is a measurement tool and not a proposal for the encoding.
The change of format for stored inventories is not designed in detail: which of the two ways, what the recovery check does with old files, and what a run in review does.
The estimate for the manifest file of each capture job (Linux job at 66.6% of 8 MiB, 10,000 profiles at about 15,400 captures) comes from the combined manifest, not from real job files.

The rows are not less code (about 520 lines in the prototype replace about 200) and a row is harder to read than a record. The maintainer asked for 'simpler'; the text says this openly, but the maintainer can still judge that the rows are not the simple way that the note asked for.

The new term 'manifest' (terms.patch.json of the first agent) gets a tooltip at each use in the whole page. The check passes on this copy; the coordinator must confirm that it passes after the merge with the other lanes.

The lead and the stats at the top of 40-data-storage.html and the gzip sentence beside D-RUN-03 in 25-run-load.html are outside this lane and still carry the numbers of r1 (for example the stop at 5,260 with no note about changed captures).
